transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
My head just feels cloudy. I’ll look at a board packet or a vendor email and kind of stare at it—I can’t decide even simple things I used to handle quickly.
Along with this cloudy feeling, have you been feeling persistently down or depressed?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. Mostly I’ve just noticed the cloudy feeling and not being able to get through things like I normally do.
Have you found yourself losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah. I haven’t wanted to go to my dance class, or look at the little galleries like I usually do. Even cooking Sunday food for my family—I just haven’t felt like it, and those things normally make me feel like myself.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
About two weeks, I think. It started around when my husband retired and was suddenly home all day—first my energy and confidence changed, and then this low, cloudy feeling.
How has your sleep been over these past two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my sleep, to be honest.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past two weeks?
My eating’s been off. Coffee and a few bites will carry me most of the day, then at night I just pick at tortillas or sweets, without really enjoying any of it.
Have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or feeling guilty about things lately?

Yeah. I keep thinking I let the residents down. I spoke too big and promised things before I’d really checked the money. Nobody’s said I ruined anything, but I still feel like I should’ve known better.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or wished that you wouldn't wake up?
A few mornings, I’ve had this scary thought that maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. But I don’t want to hurt myself, and I don’t have any plan.
